transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Mr. Dubois, thank you for waiting for me. I wanted to come by and talk to you about the bleeding we saw in your scans this morning.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I feel very weak. Everything is spinning. What is happening?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know this has been a frightening morning. I am very sorry that this happened. Our team made a mistake with your medication, and as a result, you had an internal bleed that required the emergency procedure.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: A mistake? What do you mean a mistake? I took the medicine you gave me.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I apologize. We didn't get the dosage right, and it caused the complication.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You are saying it was the medicine? But I felt fine until I woke up with this pain. C'est inadmissible. How can this happen in a hospital?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You do not understand. I have lived my whole life with discipline. I follow the rules. And now I am lying here because someone was careless with my life.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I hear you. We are monitoring you very closely now to make sure you are stable.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Who did this? Was it you? Or a nurse? Who was the one who forgot the dose?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: There was some confusion with the ordering process, and things didn't go quite right with the prescription.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Confusion. That is a very small word for a very big bleed. I want to know exactly what you gave me. Which drug? How much?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We had an issue with the amount that was entered into the system.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You are avoiding the question. I am not a child. I want the truth. Was it a ten-fold dose? A hundred? I can see you are hiding the details.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'm just trying to make sure we focus on the fact that you are stable now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I do not care about being stable if I cannot trust my doctor. Je me sens humilié. To be treated like a casualty of a clerical error.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'm sorry you feel that way.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You are not sorry I feel this way. You are sorry you were caught.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I really am sorry for the error. My team and I take full responsibility for it.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: And now? What happens tomorrow? Do I stay in this bed for another week because of this mistake?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We'll keep a close eye on your blood work and we'll see how the numbers look.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That is not an answer. Do I need more surgery? Do I need more blood?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We will just have to wait and see how you recover over the next few hours.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: This is not how a plan works. I want a written report of what happened.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'll look into that for you.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: When? Today? Tomorrow?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'll see if I can get something sorted.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You are very vague. You apologize, but you do not explain and you do not plan. It is very frustrating.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You keep saying that. But you are looking at your watch.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I do have another patient who is currently unstable, so I really have to get back to the ward.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: So I am the "stable" one and therefore I am no longer your priority?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: That is not what I meant. I just need to check on someone.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Go then. Go to your other patient. I will be here, bleeding and waiting for an answer that never comes.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I will come back later.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Please. Just go.

H.justification: Resident uses rushing language ('I really have to get back to the ward') and shows defensive escalation when the patient expresses frustration.

E.justification: While the resident initially mentions a 'mistake with medication', they pivot to platitudes like 'confusion with the ordering process' and 'things didn't go quite right' when asked for specific facts, and never check for comprehension.

A.justification: Resident uses direct apology language ('I am very sorry', 'I apologize') and explicitly states 'My team and I take full responsibility for it' while maintaining this under pushback.

R.justification: Resident relies on generic validation ('I understand', 'I hear you') and fails to name specific emotions or engage with the patient's emotional bids regarding their dignity and trust.

T.justification: Resident provides only placeholders ('wait and see', 'look into that', 'see if I can get something sorted') with no timelines, patient role, or prevention strategy.
